english_verification.review_scope: Representative current-Mod opening history and English flavour names; fixed-revision offline English Wiki history snippet for the Akalate's separation and Garlas-kel Palace of Magi; no exhaustive mission-tree audit. Native English idea names/descriptions were compared by localisation key with the current Mod. Wide line ranges locate separately read passages, not exhaustive coverage. No formal validator, build, browser or gameplay test was run.
unresolved: The Wiki passage supports the 1428 separation and successor context, but does not certify every current mission effect or formation condition.
The later F52/F53 formation branches were checked against local text scope, not exhaustively replayed for reachability.

rationale.campaign_length: The F22 scripts define 41 direct missions; later formables are counted separately.
rationale.colonization: The missions are not an overseas-colonisation campaign.
rationale.complexity: Wars, sects, mage resources and formation decisions run in parallel.
rationale.dark_story: Memories of persecution, religious assassination and revenge run through the story.
rationale.difficulty: Multiple fronts demand careful pacing; this has not been confirmed through play.
rationale.diplomacy: There are allied and subject routes, but the core remains military.
rationale.early_pressure: The opening is caught between a powerful Sun Elf state and surrounding powers.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: The mage estate, djinn relics and Wish magic occupy an important part of the main route.
rationale.narrative_density: Rebellion, restoration, religious politics and mage politics form a continuous sequence of turns.
rationale.tall_play: The Palace of Magi and urban reconstruction matter, but are not the sole loop.
rationale.trade_economy: Rebuilding ancient cities and magical industries supports the unification campaign.
rationale.warfare: Restoring Bahar and unifying Bulwar require continuous warfare.

identity.appearance: A Bahari human Old Sun Cult monarchy in 1444; Baharšes is a mission name override, not an independent Tag.
identity.formation_scope: It can optionally form Surakes (F52) or Mushasharām (F53); the different decisions change Tag and mission tree and are not equivalent.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text:
The legacy of few individuals in recent Bulwari history is as divisive as that of Dartaxes szel-Farramaz. Born in 1401 AA to a minor Barkabti noble family hailing from Farramaz, then one of the northern provinces of Birzartanšes, he spent his youth at court in Birsartansbar. Showing a talent for command and an aptitude for military strategy, he rose to the rank of general at the tender age of eighteen. Proving his mettle against enemy forces during the Baharkandi-Birsartanšesi War, his exceptional victory at the battle of Habqez cemented his reputation. This would prove to be a mixed blessing, however, as he received the thankless task of subduing the Great Rebellion and reestablishing order in the northern provinces ravaged by the Decades of Devastation.
But loyal service to inept monarch is seldom rewarded, leading to a deep estrangement and the eventual rebellion of Dartaxes himself, who gathered an unlikely coalition of soldiers loyal to him, provincial nobles with connections to his family, and, most importantly, the fanatically devout Šebhuliam sect. While he failed to overthrow Arantir of Birzartanšes, he managed to forge his own realm out of the borderlands between Birzartanšes and Baharkand. Many hopes were pinned upon him, the first independent human Akal in Bahar since the fall of the Phoenix Empire. Yet it all came crashing down when in 1484 the forces of Birzartanšes reconquered this fledgling realm and he was burned alive in the ruins of the Šebhuliam fortress of Azka-szel-Parkellu.

description.text:
For several millennia, the seemingly tranquil lake Garlas hid an astounding secret beneath the salt pans along its shores.
Buried beneath the surface lie the ruins of Is-Kuršag, one of the four capitals of the djinni Radiant Sultanates. Its rediscovery during the mid-15th century AA led to the establishment of an Eka, a bulwari mage academy devoted to the study of genie magic which developed into one of the foremost institutions of bulwari magic as a whole.
This Eka-Uššupammun, or ‘Palace whose Foundations Hide Knowledge’ swiftly became one of the major support pillars of Dartaxâgerdim and survived its downfall by seeking shelter under the wings of a resurgent harpy queendom that took over the mountainous eastern provinces of the akalate.
Mages trained within these walls tend to swiftly rise to prestigious positions and often become revered masters of the arcane arts. Yet without fail they refuse to divulge details of their time spend at the Eka to outsiders, lending it an air of mystery and igniting the imagination of conspiracy theorists across Bulwar, who speculate about everything from a secret cabal of genie cultists ruling over the academy to a hidden gate to the elemental plane of air or the incorporeal spirits of several god-kings trapped in a wishblade stored in the catacombs of the Eka.

description.text:
The Decades of Devastation, as the name implies, had a catastrophic effect on the lands of Bahar. Like a corroding acid the constant border skirmishes, rampant banditry and open neglect of infrastructure and institutions alike led to a dissolution of societal structures once thought inviolate.
Not only the people of Bahar struggled to cling to a semblance of normalcy, trying to earn their livelyhood while armies clashed all around them. Those armies themselves suffered from the rampant institutional collapse as well, lacking secure supply lines and reliable access to the necessary Tools of their bloody trade.
One of the often overlooked aspects of Dartaxes’ military genius was therefore his astute understanding of logistics and the development of an ingeniously flexible supply system primarily based on local sympathizers and supplemented by the remnants of the old Birsartanšesi military administration that he suborned for his purposes.

description.text:
‘The light does not cower from the dark, it dispels all shadow and burns away all falsehood - how can you consider yourself devoted to Surakel's Light if you are unwilling to follow the example He set and stride forth to vanquish the Malevolent Dark!’
     -Fragment of a Šebhuliam harangue

The Šebhuliam were founded by Ašuru Telissaku, son of a preacher from the Cult of Mourning called Xakkim. After the Purge of Medurubar, Ašuru and his father fled north. While Xakkim’s followers became the Cult of Purity, Ašuru and his acolytes built the fortress of Azka-szel-Parkellu, the ‘Fortress of those who seek Purity’, in the mountain of Kuzak over the ruins of the harpy roost of Tounafira. His followers became the Green Helmets, a moniker referring to their habit of tying green cloth as a symbol of faithful purity around their helmets when they left their mountain fastness on their initiation missions to assassinate sun elven officials or other proponents of the New Sun Cult.

description.text:
Bulwar has no lack of tragedies in its long history. One of the more recent ones gave rise to the Cult of Purity. The Purge of Medurubar was a massacre of recalcitrant adherents of sun cults that rejected the doctrinal consensus reached at the council of Brasan. Originally a shelter for those who rejected the theological reforms pushed through by Taelarios and his allies amongst the clergy, the city of Medurubar soon became a target for the more zealous adherents of the new status quo.
The adherents of the Cult of Mourning, a cult risen in the wake of the destruction wrought by the Red Xhaz all along the lower Suran, were among those who hoped to practice their faith undisturbed within the walls of Medurubar. Once the Order of the Zenith raised their blades to purge Medurubar from heresy, only few managed to escape the massacre.
One of these survivors was the preacher Xakkim and his followers, who fled north into the wilderness of the Šad Kuz and into Bahar, where they founded the Cult of Purity, whose central doctrine is the concept that the people of Bulwar have to endure tragedies and suffering due to the spiritual corruption of Surakel’s Garden, and that only by ritually cleansing it may it thrive again.
Aside from the Cult of Mourning, other venerable cults native to Bahar such as the Cult of Truth or the Cult of the Mother have influenced the Genesis of the Cult of Purity, which in turn birthed the Green Helmets or Šebhuliam.

description.text:
Modesty, restraint or low self-esteem are not character traits commonly associated with gnollish rulers, and Uak ‘the Tremendous’ was no exception. He did not waste any time once his pack had carved out a sizable chunk of Bahar for their new kingdom and began to work on his legacy by founding a new city on the banks of the Našra to serve as his capital. With typical gnollish bluntness and flair for self-aggrandizing he named this city Akal-Uakbar - the City of King Uak.
Over the many centuries since its founding, that name has been shortened to Akal-Uak. Unlike most other major Bulwari cities that are found on the flat floodplains of major rivers, Akal-Uak stretches across several hills, with each hill being the center of a city-within-the city, a last remnant of gnollish tendencies to place some distance between sub-packs within a large gnollish horde to avoid unnecessary conflict born from rivalries or mere boredom. For the longest time Akal-Uak has been the undisputed hegemon of the Našra valley, and perennial rival of Aqatbar for the title of capital of Bahar. Only in the last centuries it had to cede its preeminent role to Birsartansbar.
It comes as no surprise then, that the aristocrats of Akal-Uak were quick to throw their support behind Dartaxes when he first secured the city and its environs for his master after the first battle of Habqez, and became its true king after defeating Arantir of Birsartanšes in the second battle of Habqez, turning it into the capital of his newborn akalate after the successful Great Rebellion.

description.text:
The gnollish pack of Uak, like those of his compatriots, brought suffering and despair to Surakel's Garden, but that is not all they brought. Uak carried with him a memento of his homeland on the other side of the Salahad, a couple of Hašitu seedlings, or Tealwood trees as the Cannorians call them. Planted in a sheltered valley near Akal-Uak, they formed a large Tealwood forest over time - the last of its kind as the lands these trees hailed from were swallowed by the Shadow Swamp in the centuries that have passed since.

Local artisans have long known that the sap collected from these trees hardens into a teal coloured amber when exposed to air and sunlight and built a thriving industry around it. This Tealwood amber is surprisingly pliant in the hands of skilled artists and intricate jewelry as well as small sculptures crafted from it are highly sought after all across Bulwar and beyond.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid this route if you do not want multi-front wars, radical religious factions and mage politics.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Win the opening survival and revenge wars in Bahar, organise mage and religious institutions in the middle game, then choose the country's post-unification form for Bulwar.
player_overview.overview: Dartaxâgerdim is an Old Sun Cult state that broke free from Sun Elf rule. You must reclaim cities in Bahar and Bulwar, shelter refugees, rebuild mage and djinn legacies, and find a new order between the Green Helmets, religious diversity and monarchy. It is both a revolt against oppression and a story that can be consumed by revenge and sectarian hatred, with different formable directions in the late game.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy human revolt, religious reform, magical revival and a long Bulwari conquest campaign.
signature_features: Resistance to Sun Elf rule and revival of the Old Sun Cult run through the mission narrative.
Rebuilding the Palace of Magi and studying djinn legacies makes war and magical institutions develop together.
Baharšes is only a name override; Surakes and Mushasharām are the distinct formable countries.
player_overview.tagline: Overthrow the Sun Elf order, then decide whom human light will illuminate.

reasons: Tension between human revolt and religious diversity gives the campaign a strong narrative core.
Mage and djinn legacies create a distinctive magical-state route.
F52 and F53 offer different late-game forms.
warnings: The Green Helmets and mage politics cast a clear shadow over the revolt narrative.

positive_indicators: The mission text explicitly shelters refugees.
The route commemorates victims of different wars and persecutions.
Later missions support coexistence among several Old Sun Cult traditions.
values.rationale: Sheltering refugees, rebuilding Bahar and respecting local Old Sun Cult traditions serve the public good; Green Helmet assassinations and collective hatred of Sun Elves reduce dignity and restraint. Conquest and monarchy are not scored as negatives by themselves.
red_flags: The Green Helmets expand their influence through assassinations of Sun Elf officials.
The anti-oppression narrative carries collective hatred of elves.
